questions.title: Serve in FIFO Order
questions.description:
The program scaffolding (input reading and main) is already set up for you. Implement only this function:

    def serve_order(values):

Enqueue every value into a deque-based queue, then dequeue everything (popleft) and return the serving order as a list — the FIFO order.

Input Format:
Line 1: n, the number of values.
Line 2: n integers.

Output Format:
One line with the values in serving order, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000
-1000000 <= value <= 1000000
questions.sourcecode:
from collections import deque
import sys


def read_lines():
    return [ln.strip() for ln in sys.stdin.read().split('\n') if ln.strip() != '']


def serve_order(values):
    q = deque(values)
    out = []
    while q:
        out.append(q.popleft())
    return out


def main():
    lines = read_lines()
    values = list(map(int, lines[1].split()))
    print(' '.join(map(str, serve_order(values))))


main()

from collections import deque
import sys


def read_lines():
    return [ln.strip() for ln in sys.stdin.read().split('\n') if ln.strip() != '']


def pop_ends(values):
    dq = deque(values)
    left = dq.popleft()
    right = dq.pop()
    return left, right


def main():
    lines = read_lines()
    values = list(map(int, lines[1].split()))

    print(left, right)


main()

questions.title: Hot Potato Survivor
questions.description:
Children stand in a circle playing hot potato: the potato is passed p-1 times, and the child holding it then leaves the circle. Play repeats until one child remains.

The program scaffolding (input reading and main) is already set up for you. Implement only this function:

    def survivor(names, p):

Simulate with a queue: for each round, rotate the queue p-1 times (popleft then append) and then remove the holder (popleft). Return the survivor's name.

Input Format:
Line 1: n and p, space-separated (p >= 1).
Line 2: n names, space-separated (single words, in circle order starting anywhere).

Output Format:
One line with the surviving name.

Constraints:

questions.sourcecode:
from collections import deque
import sys


def read_lines():
    return [ln.strip() for ln in sys.stdin.read().split('\n') if ln.strip() != '']


def survivor(names, p):
    q = deque(names)
    while len(q) > 1:
        for _ in range(p - 1):
            q.append(q.popleft())
        q.popleft()
    return q[0]


def main():
    lines = read_lines()
    p = int(lines[0].split()[1])
    names = lines[1].split()
    print(survivor(names, p))


main()

questions.sourcecode:
from collections import deque
import sys


def read_lines():
    return [ln.strip() for ln in sys.stdin.read().split('\n') if ln.strip() != '']


def diverted(cars, k):
    q = deque(cars)
    i = 0
    out = []
    while q:
        car = q.popleft()
        i += 1
        if i % k == 0:
            out.append(car)
    return out


def main():
    lines = read_lines()
    k = int(lines[0].split()[1])
    cars = lines[1].split()
    print(' '.join(diverted(cars, k)))


main()

questions.title: Round Robin Job Finish Order
questions.description:
A CPU scheduler runs jobs round-robin: each job gets quantum time units per turn; a job that still has remaining work rejoins the back of the queue.

The program scaffolding (input reading and main) is already set up for you. Implement only this function:

    def completion_order(bursts, quantum):

bursts are the CPU bursts of jobs indexed 0..n-1. Simulate with a deque and return the list of job indices in the order they finish.

Input Format:
Line 1: n and quantum, space-separated (quantum >= 1).
Line 2: n integers (the bursts, each >= 1).

Output Format:
One line with the finishing indices, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100
1 <= quantum <= 20
1 <= burst <= 50
questions.sourcecode:
from collections import deque
import sys


def read_lines():
    return [ln.strip() for ln in sys.stdin.read().split('\n') if ln.strip() != '']


def completion_order(bursts, quantum):
    q = deque(range(len(bursts)))
    left = list(bursts)
    done = []
    while q:
        i = q.popleft()
        step = left[i] if left[i] < quantum else quantum
        left[i] -= step
        if left[i] == 0:
            done.append(i)
        else:
            q.append(i)
    return done


def main():
    lines = read_lines()
    quantum = int(lines[0].split()[1])
    bursts = list(map(int, lines[1].split()))
    print(' '.join(map(str, completion_order(bursts, quantum))))


main()

questions.sourcecode:
from collections import deque
import sys


def read_lines():
    return [ln.strip() for ln in sys.stdin.read().split('\n') if ln.strip() != '']


def start_station(petrol, dist):
    total = 0
    curr = 0
    start = 0
    for i in range(len(petrol)):
        d = petrol[i] - dist[i]
        total += d
        curr += d
        if curr < 0:
            start = i + 1
            curr = 0
    return start if total >= 0 else -1


def main():
    lines = read_lines()
    petrol = list(map(int, lines[1].split()))
    dist = list(map(int, lines[2].split()))
    print(start_station(petrol, dist))


main()

from collections import deque
import sys


def read_lines():
    return [ln.strip() for ln in sys.stdin.read().split('\n') if ln.strip() != '']


def interleaved(values):
    first = deque(values[: len(values) // 2])
    second = deque(values[len(values) // 2 :])
    out = []
    while first:
        out.append(first.popleft())
        out.append(second.popleft())
    return out


def main():
    lines = read_lines()
    values = list(map(int, lines[1].split()))
    print(' '.join(map(str, interleaved(values))))


main()
